Travelling-salesman route through a set of nodes

Source: R/routing.R
ox_route_tsp.Rd

Finds a short route through nodes over the street network, in the spirit of sfnetworks::st_network_travel(). Network distances between all pairs of stops are computed in the Rust core (one Dijkstra per stop, so one-way streets are respected via the asymmetric cost matrix), the visiting order is solved with an iterated local search, and each leg is expanded back into a shortest path with its street geometry.

Usage

ox_route_tsp(
  g,
  nodes,
  weight = "length",
  start = 1,
  end = start,
  method = c("ils", "nn")
)

Arguments

g

An osm_graph.

nodes

Node osmids to visit (at least 2, no duplicates), e.g. from ox_nearest_nodes().

weight

Edge column used as weight. Default "length"; use "travel_time" after ox_add_edge_travel_times() for fastest routes.

start

Index into nodes of the first stop. Default 1.

end

Index into nodes of the final stop. The default (end = start) gives a closed tour that returns to the start; end = NULL leaves the final stop free (an open route); any other index pins the route's end.

method

"ils" (default, nearest-neighbour + iterated local search) or "nn" (nearest-neighbour only).

Value

An sf tibble with one row per leg of the route: leg, from and to (node osmids), cost (network distance in weight units), a list-column path of the osmids traversed, and the leg's LINESTRING geometry. The total route cost is sum(out$cost).

Details

The default solver builds a nearest-neighbour tour and polishes it with an iterated local search: a descent over or-opt (segment relocation), swap and 2-opt moves — every move evaluated exactly on the asymmetric cost matrix — restarted from double-bridge perturbations, keeping the best tour found. The search is deterministic (an internal fixed-seed RNG drives the perturbations, leaving R's RNG untouched). It routinely finds the global optimum for small stop counts, but optimality is not guaranteed (the TSP is NP-hard). method = "nn" skips the improvement and keeps the raw nearest-neighbour order.

Examples

g <- example_osm_graph()
stops <- c(1, 4, 13, 16, 6)
route <- ox_route_tsp(g, stops)
route
#> Simple feature collection with 5 features and 5 fields
#> Geometry type: LINESTRING
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 0 ymin: 0 xmax: 300 ymax: 300
#> Projected CRS: WGS 84 / Pseudo-Mercator
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>     leg  from    to  cost path                                geometry
#>   <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <list>                      <LINESTRING [m]>
#> 1     1     1     6   200 <int [3]>              (0 0, 100 0, 100 100)
#> 2     2     6     4   300 <int [4]>     (100 100, 0 100, 0 200, 0 300)
#> 3     3     4    16   300 <int [4]> (0 300, 100 300, 200 300, 300 300)
#> 4     4    16    13   300 <int [4]> (300 300, 300 200, 300 100, 300 0)
#> 5     5    13     1   300 <int [4]>         (300 0, 200 0, 100 0, 0 0)
sum(route$cost)
#> [1] 1400
